Characters created by Mark Twain.Huck Finn: His 1884 adventure has been repeatedly banned, and Hemingway said all American literature comes from it.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Becky Thatcher: Becky Thatcher is the judge's daughter and Tom's sweetheart, and is lost with him in McDougal's Cave.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Aunt Polly: Aunt Polly is Tom's guardian aunt, who punishes him by making him whitewash the fence and is forever outfoxed.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Jim: Jim is the runaway enslaved man who journeys with Huck down the Mississippi, and is the moral center of the novel.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Sid Sawyer: Sid Sawyer is Tom's goody-goody half-brother, who tells on him whenever he can.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Pap Finn: Pap Finn is Huck's violent, drunken father, who kidnaps him for his money and drives him to flee.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Muff Potter: Muff Potter is the drunken local falsely accused of murder in Tom Sawyer, until Tom testifies.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Widow Douglas: Widow Douglas takes Huck in and tries to 'sivilize' him with clean clothes and lessons, and he hates it.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Joe Harper: Joe Harper is Tom's friend, who joins him in running away to be a pirate on Jackson's Island.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Miss Watson: Miss Watson, the Widow Douglas's sister, owns Jim and is the reason he runs away.
Characters created by Mark Twain.The Duke: The Duke and the King are con men who join Huck and Jim's raft, staging bogus Shakespeare along the river.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Atticus Finch: Atticus Finch is the lawyer of Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, and the name Finch is a trap for Finn.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Scout Finch: Scout Finch narrates Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird in Alabama, so she's not Twain's.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Boo Radley: Boo Radley is the reclusive neighbor who saves the children in To Kill a Mockingbird, by Harper Lee.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Holden Caulfield: Holden Caulfield narrates J. D. Salinger's The Catcher in the Rye, so he's not Twain's.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Jay Gatsby: Jay Gatsby is F. Scott Fitzgerald's mysterious millionaire, who stares at a green light across the water.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Ishmael: Ishmael is Melville's narrator in Moby-Dick, and the novel opens with 'Call me Ishmael'.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Rip Van Winkle: Rip Van Winkle is Washington Irving's man who sleeps for twenty years in the Catskills.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Ichabod Crane: Ichabod Crane is Washington Irving's schoolteacher chased by the Headless Horseman in Sleepy Hollow.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Hester Prynne: Hester Prynne is Nathaniel Hawthorne's heroine, forced to wear the scarlet letter A in The Scarlet Letter.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Natty Bumppo: Natty Bumppo, called Hawkeye, is James Fenimore Cooper's frontiersman in the Leatherstocking Tales.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Jo March: Jo March is Louisa May Alcott's writer heroine in Little Women, not Twain's.
Characters created by Mark Twain.Lennie Small: Lennie Small is John Steinbeck's gentle giant in Of Mice and Men, not Twain's.

Things that are triangular.Yield sign: It's one of few road signs shaped like a downward-pointing triangle, which makes it stand out from the many octagons, circles and diamonds.
Things that are triangular.Pizza slice: A classic wedge cut from a round pie; the pointed tip is the center of the pizza, where the crust is usually softest.
Things that are triangular.Dorito: Doritos were created at Disneyland in the 1960s, where a restaurant fried leftover tortillas into triangular chips, and the idea took off nationwide.
Things that are triangular.Toblerone: Its triangular peaks are often said to echo the Matterhorn, and the bar was created in Bern, Switzerland, in 1908.
Things that are triangular.Coat hanger: The familiar triangle shape works because it spreads a garment's weight over the shoulders, and a wire version is said to date to about 1903.
Things that are triangular.Musical triangle: This steel percussion rod, bent into a triangle with one open corner, produces a bright ring that carries over a full orchestra.
Things that are triangular.Guitar pick: A guitar pick is a rounded triangle, with its thickness changing the tone, and a thicker pick gives a rounder sound.
Things that are triangular.Samosa: Samosas likely originated in the Middle East, and travelled to South Asia centuries ago, where the stuffed triangle became a classic snack.
Things that are triangular.Pennant: Long triangular flags, called pennants, flew from medieval lances and ships, and baseball borrowed the word for championship flags.
Things that are triangular.Pool rack: The triangle racks 15 object balls tightly for the break; its shape is why billiards players call the start 'racking up'.
Things that are triangular.Sailboat sail: The triangular jib or mainsail lets a boat sail at an angle toward the wind, thanks to the lift it makes like a plane's wing.
Things that are triangular.Stop sign: It's a trap: the stop sign is an octagon, with eight sides, chosen so drivers can recognize it even from behind or when snowed over.
Things that are triangular.Dice: A standard die is a cube with six square faces, though some role-playing dice have triangular faces, like the pointed d20.
Things that are triangular.Coin: Coins are nearly always round, which makes them roll easily and wear evenly, though a few countries have minted polygonal ones.
Things that are triangular.Envelope: The flap is a triangle, but the envelope as a whole is a rectangle, a good example of a part that fits when the whole doesn't.
Things that are triangular.Book: A book is a rectangle with a spine and covers, and its shape is a set of folded sheets, not a triangle in any way.
Things that are triangular.Clock: Most clocks are round with a circular face, though their hands sweep out thin triangles at times.
Things that are triangular.Domino: A domino is a rectangle twice as long as it is wide, with a line splitting it into two square halves.
Things that are triangular.Credit card: All bank cards follow an international standard of about 85.6 by 54 millimeters, a rounded rectangle.
Things that are triangular.Pizza box: Pizza is round but its box is square, which makes it easy to stack and cheap to fold from a single cardboard sheet.
Things that are triangular.Tennis ball: Tennis balls are spheres of hollow rubber covered in felt, and the curved seam pattern of the cover comes from two dumbbell-shaped pieces.
Things that are triangular.Door: A standard door is a tall rectangle, because it needs to fit people through while remaining easy to frame in a wall.
Things that are triangular.Window: Windows are usually rectangular since sheet glass and wall framing are easiest to build with straight edges.
Things that are triangular.Stamp: The first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black of 1840, was a rectangle, and only a few later ones were triangular, like Cape of Good Hope's.

Things that fit in a pocket.Key: The pin tumbler lock that most keys fit descends from an ancient Egyptian design, and a modern key's cuts match pin heights.
Things that fit in a pocket.Coin: Coins have been pocket change since the first ones were minted in Lydia, now Turkey, nearly 2,700 years ago.
Things that fit in a pocket.Smartphone: A modern phone has more computing power than the computers that guided Apollo 11 to the Moon, and it still fits in a jeans pocket.
Things that fit in a pocket.Lip balm: Lip balm is often a wax and oil mix, and a stick is small enough to vanish in laundry, where it can melt in the dryer.
Things that fit in a pocket.Wallet: Wallets once held coins and notes, and the first banknotes appeared in China around the 11th century.
Things that fit in a pocket.Pen: The ballpoint pen was patented by Hungarian László Bíró in 1938, and its tiny rolling ball delivers ink without smearing.
Things that fit in a pocket.Guitar pick: Picks are often sold as plectrums, and many guitarists keep a few in a pocket, since they are easily lost.
Things that fit in a pocket.Pack of gum: Chewing gum goes back thousands of years, and ancient Greeks chewed mastic resin, from a tree.
Things that fit in a pocket.Marble: Marbles are children's toys from antiquity, with clay ones found in ancient Egypt, and the cat's eye pattern is a glass classic.
Things that fit in a pocket.USB stick: The first flash drives went on sale in 2000, holding eight megabytes, a tiny fraction of what a modern one holds.
Things that fit in a pocket.Tissue: A pocket tissue is a handy invention, and Kleenex was first marketed in the 1920s as a cold cream remover.
Things that fit in a pocket.Dice: A pair of dice can be carried in a pocket, and the oldest found, from about 3000 BCE, were in Iran.
Things that fit in a pocket.Earbuds: Earbuds in a pocket get tangled by themselves, thanks to random knotting that scientists have tested in boxes with string.
Things that fit in a pocket.Laptop: A laptop is a trap: even the thinnest models are too big and fragile to fit in a pocket, though some fold small.
Things that fit in a pocket.Bowling ball: A bowling ball weighs up to 16 pounds and about 8.5 inches across, so it would drag down any pair of pants.
Things that fit in a pocket.Watermelon: Watermelon is about 92 percent water, and a whole one is far too big for a pocket, weighing several kilograms.
Things that fit in a pocket.Guitar: A guitar has a body about the size of a small child, and is clearly too big for a pocket, but a ukulele may come close.
Things that fit in a pocket.Toaster: A toaster is a kitchen appliance with a cord, much too bulky to put in a pocket.
Things that fit in a pocket.Golf umbrella: A golf umbrella has a canopy up to 60 inches across and is an oversized one that covers two people.
Things that fit in a pocket.Pillow: A pillow is bulky, even if it squishes down a bit, and it is too big to fit in any normal pocket.
Things that fit in a pocket.Basketball: A basketball is about 24 centimeters across, far too large for pockets.
Things that fit in a pocket.Skateboard: A skateboard deck is usually about 80 centimeters long, so it cannot fit in a pocket.
Things that fit in a pocket.Microwave: The microwave oven was invented after Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting in his pocket in the 1940s, near a radar tube.
Things that fit in a pocket.Tennis racket: A racket is about 68 centimeters long, so it is much too long for any pocket.

Chinese New Year traditions.Red envelope: Red envelopes, hongbao, hold money for children and unmarried relatives. Red is the color of luck, and amounts often avoid the number four.
Chinese New Year traditions.Dragon dance: A dragon dance needs a team carrying a long, segmented dragon on poles. The longer the dragon, the more luck it is thought to bring.
Chinese New Year traditions.Lion dance: Lion dancers, two per costume, leap to scare off evil spirits. Shopkeepers hang lettuce and a red envelope for the lion to 'eat' for fortune.
Chinese New Year traditions.Firecrackers: Legend says firecrackers scared away a monster named Nian. They are now restricted in many Chinese cities for safety and air quality.
Chinese New Year traditions.Dumplings: Dumplings, shaped like ancient gold ingots, symbolize wealth. In northern China families make them together on New Year's Eve.
Chinese New Year traditions.Lanterns: The festival ends 15 days later with the Lantern Festival, when red lanterns carry riddles for guests to solve.
Chinese New Year traditions.Spring couplets: Spring couplets are poetic red banners pasted on doors, with calligraphy wishing the household good fortune and happiness.
Chinese New Year traditions.Zodiac animal: The Chinese zodiac runs on a 12-year cycle of animals, from rat to pig. According to legend, the animals raced across a river to earn their places.
Chinese New Year traditions.Mandarin oranges: Mandarins are gifted in pairs because the Cantonese word for 'orange' sounds like 'gold', and 'tangerine' like 'luck'.
Chinese New Year traditions.Reunion dinner: The reunion dinner on New Year's Eve is the most important meal of the year, drawing the largest annual human migration, the chunyun travel rush.
Chinese New Year traditions.Mooncake: Mooncakes are for the Mid-Autumn Festival in September or October. They're eaten under the full moon, not for the lunar new year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Jack-o'-lantern: A carved pumpkin lantern is a Halloween custom from Irish and American tradition, and isn't part of the Lunar New Year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Menorah: The menorah is a candelabrum for Hanukkah, a Jewish festival of lights, not Chinese New Year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Easter egg: Decorated eggs belong to the Christian spring holiday of Easter, a different calendar from the lunar new year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Christmas tree: The Christmas tree began in Germany centuries ago, and it is a December tradition rather than a lunar new year one.
Chinese New Year traditions.Pumpkin pie: Pumpkin pie is an American Thanksgiving dessert, not a Chinese New Year treat, where dumplings and sticky rice cakes reign.
Chinese New Year traditions.Shamrock: The shamrock is a St. Patrick's Day symbol of Ireland, which has no relation to Chinese New Year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Maypole: A maypole is danced around on May Day in European spring festivals, not at the lunar new year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Dreidel: A dreidel is a spinning top for Hanukkah. Like the red envelopes, it involves gifts of coins, but it's Jewish, not Chinese.
Chinese New Year traditions.Cupid: Cupid belongs to Valentine's Day. It's a Western figure, though Chinese Qixi has its own romance legend.
Chinese New Year traditions.Sugar skull: Sugar skulls are decorated for Mexico's Day of the Dead, honoring departed loved ones, not for Chinese New Year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Rangoli: Rangoli are colorful floor patterns made at Diwali in India, using powder or flower petals, not at Chinese New Year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Dragon boat race: Dragon boat racing belongs to the Duanwu Festival in early summer, remembering poet Qu Yuan, not the new year.
Chinese New Year traditions.Eggnog: Eggnog is a creamy Christmas drink, served in December, not part of the lunar new year feast.

Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Canada Day: Always July 1, marking the 1867 confederation that created Canada.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Guy Fawkes Night: Always November 5, recalling the Gunpowder Plot of 1605 and the arrest of Guy Fawkes.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Cinco de Mayo: Always May 5, marking the 1862 Battle of Puebla, not Mexican independence, which is September 16.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Fourth of July: Always July 4, marking the 1776 Declaration of Independence.

Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Mother's Day: The second Sunday in May in the US, so the date varies each year.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Father's Day: The third Sunday in June in the US, so the date varies each year.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Chinese New Year: Falls on the new moon between January 21 and February 20, so the date moves.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Mardi Gras: Falls 47 days before Easter, so the date changes each year.
Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Passover: Begins on 15 Nisan in the Hebrew calendar, so it moves on the Gregorian calendar.

Holidays on the same Gregorian date ever.Holi: Falls on the full moon in spring, so the date varies each year.

Parts of a classic snowman.Carrot nose: Frosty's song mentions a button nose, but the carrot has become the image: a bright orange pointer.
Parts of a classic snowman.Top hat: Frosty came to life when a magic silk hat was placed on his head, so this accessory is the key part of the legend.
Parts of a classic snowman.Scarf: A cozy detail added to many snowmen, usually knitted and tied around the neck.
Parts of a classic snowman.Coal eyes: Pieces of coal are the classic eyes, though pebbles and buttons are also used.
Parts of a classic snowman.Twig arms: Twigs are the classic arms, and the pose is often held out to the sides.
Parts of a classic snowman.Coal buttons: Coal in a row down the front gives a cheerful button look.
Parts of a classic snowman.Corncob pipe: Frosty's pipe is famous from the song, a hint of old-time winter scenery.
Parts of a classic snowman.Snowballs: Three big rolled balls of snow stack to form the body, and the oldest known snowman picture is from 1380.
Parts of a classic snowman.Coal mouth: A curved line of small pieces of coal gives the classic grin.
Parts of a classic snowman.Flip-flops: Snowmen have no feet, since they are just stacked balls, so any footwear is out.
Parts of a classic snowman.Tutu: Frosty's winter belongs to the Nutcracker's Waltz of the Snowflakes, but this ballet skirt is not part of a snowman.
Parts of a classic snowman.Bikini: The bikini is named for Bikini Atoll, where atomic tests took place in 1946, and has no place on something that melts.
Parts of a classic snowman.Wig: A hat stays on a snowman, but a wig would slide off a smooth ball of snow.
Parts of a classic snowman.Sombrero: From Spanish sombra, shade, the sombrero shades from sun, the last thing a snowman wants.
Parts of a classic snowman.Life jacket: A life jacket is for water, and the one thing a snowman fears is water in puddle form.
Parts of a classic snowman.Roller skates: Snowmen are built from three balls with no legs, so skating is not possible.
Parts of a classic snowman.Tiara: Fit for a princess, but a snowman is a commoner who wears a hat.
Parts of a classic snowman.Monocle: The monocle belongs to Mr. Peanut, who wears it with a top hat, but not to classic snowmen.
Parts of a classic snowman.Wetsuit: A wetsuit would be absurd for a creature that melts in water.
Parts of a classic snowman.Halo: Halos are for angels, and a snowman is not heavenly, though it stays pure white.
Parts of a classic snowman.Backpack: Backpacks belong to hikers, and a snowman with twig arms has no way to carry one.
Parts of a classic snowman.Earrings: Snowmen have no ears, so earrings are out.
Parts of a classic snowman.Jeans: Snowmen are not wearing trousers, since the body is simply stacked balls.
Parts of a classic snowman.Umbrella: A snowman might want an umbrella against the sun, but nobody adds one to the classic build.

Harry Potter spells.Expelliarmus: The Disarming Charm is Harry's signature spell; it knocks a wand from an opponent's hand and his final duel with Voldemort turned on it.
Harry Potter spells.Lumos: This spell lights the tip of a wand; its name is a Latin word for light, and Nox is its counter-spell.
Harry Potter spells.Nox: Nox puts out the light made by Lumos; its name is Latin for night.
Harry Potter spells.Accio: The summoning charm pulls objects to the caster; the name is Latin for I summon, and Harry used it to fetch his broom for the Triwizard task.
Harry Potter spells.Alohomora: The unlocking charm's name was reportedly inspired by a West African Sidiki word meaning friendly to thieves.
Harry Potter spells.Wingardium Leviosa: The levitation charm that Hermione corrects Ron on: it's wing-GAR-dium levi-OH-sa, not levio-SAR.
Harry Potter spells.Expecto Patronum: This spell conjures a silver guardian that repels Dementors; its form depends on the caster, such as a stag for Harry.
Harry Potter spells.Stupefy: The Stunning Spell knocks out its target; its red flash is the most common of dueling bolts, used throughout the battle at Hogwarts.
Harry Potter spells.Obliviate: The memory charm wipes recollections; Gilderoy Lockhart accidentally used it on himself in book two.
Harry Potter spells.Riddikulus: Used on boggarts to turn fear into comedy; the caster pictures something funny, like Snape in Neville's grandmother's clothes.
Harry Potter spells.Petrificus Totalus: The full body-bind curse; Hermione used it on Neville in the first book when he tried to stop them.
Harry Potter spells.Reparo: A simple mending charm for broken objects, which Hermione used to fix Harry's glasses.
Harry Potter spells.Incendio: The fire-making spell, with a name from the Latin for I set on fire.
Harry Potter spells.Abracadabra: Real-world magic word that may date to ancient Rome, once said to cure fevers when written in a shrinking triangle. Not a Potter spell, though Avada Kedavra descends from it.
Harry Potter spells.Hocus pocus: This stage-magic phrase may be a mock-Latin parody of the Catholic Mass; not a Potter spell.
Harry Potter spells.Bibbidi-bobbidi-boo: Fairy Godmother's chant from Disney's 1950 Cinderella; it earned an Oscar nomination for best song, but isn't from Hogwarts.
Harry Potter spells.Open sesame: Ali Baba's cave password from The Arabian Nights; Harry Potter's unlocking charm is Alohomora instead.
Harry Potter spells.Alakazam: A classic magician's word of unclear origin; it also names a Pokemon, but it isn't a Harry Potter spell.
Harry Potter spells.Shazam: The word that turns Billy Batson into Captain Marvel; it stands for six gods and heroes, not a Hogwarts charm.
Harry Potter spells.Sim sala bim: A magician's phrase popularised by the Danish-born illusionist Dante, who titled his stage show Sim Sala Bim; not a Hogwarts spell.
Harry Potter spells.Presto chango: Stage-magic patter meaning change quickly; Hogwarts has no such spell, but Transfiguration does the real work.
Harry Potter spells.Klaatu barada nikto: The words that stop the robot Gort in the 1951 film The Day the Earth Stood Still; pure sci-fi, not wizardry.
Harry Potter spells.Xyzzy: A magic word from the 1970s text game Colossal Cave Adventure; it became a classic programmer's in-joke.
Harry Potter spells.Kazaam: This is the title of a 1996 movie in which Shaquille O'Neal plays a genie; not a Harry Potter spell.

Hindu gods and goddesses.Ganesha: The elephant-headed god of beginnings and remover of obstacles is invoked at the start of ventures, weddings and journeys.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Lakshmi: Goddess of wealth and good fortune, she is honored at Diwali, when lamps are lit to welcome her into homes.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Vishnu: The preserver in the Hindu trinity is believed to descend to Earth as avatars, among them Rama and Krishna.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Shiva: God of destruction and renewal, he is often shown as Nataraja, dancing the cosmos into being, with the Ganges flowing from his hair.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Hanuman: The monkey god, famed for devotion to Rama, is said to have leapt across the sea to Lanka.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Kali: A fierce goddess with a garland of skulls, she destroys evil and is also revered as a loving mother.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Durga: Riding a lion or tiger, this warrior goddess defeated the buffalo demon Mahishasura, celebrated at Durga Puja.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Saraswati: Goddess of knowledge, music and learning, she is shown with a veena, and students honor her with books before exams.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Krishna: The blue-skinned god of love and compassion delivers the Bhagavad Gita's teachings to Arjuna on the battlefield.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Rama: The hero of the Ramayana, he is honored at Diwali and Ram Navami as the ideal king and a Vishnu avatar.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Brahma: The creator in the Hindu trinity has four faces, but few temples are dedicated to him, with Pushkar being the best known.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Parvati: Shiva's consort and mother of Ganesha, she embodies power and devotion, and also appears in forms like Durga.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Zeus: King of the Greek gods who wielded thunderbolts from Mount Olympus. He belongs to Greek, not Hindu, religion.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Odin: The Norse all-father gave up an eye for wisdom, and ruled Asgard in Scandinavian mythology.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Thor: The Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjolnir. He is not Hindu, though some thunder gods like Indra share traits.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Ra: The Egyptian sun god sailed his barque across the sky each day, and is Egyptian, not Hindu.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Anubis: The jackal-headed Egyptian god guided the dead and weighed hearts against a feather. He is not Hindu.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Quetzalcoatl: This Aztec feathered serpent god was credited with bringing knowledge and maize to humans.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Amaterasu: Japan's Shinto sun goddess is the legendary ancestor of the imperial family. She is not Hindu.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Loki: Norse trickster, he is a shapeshifter who even gave birth to Odin's eight-legged horse Sleipnir.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Isis: Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood whose worship spread across the Roman Empire. She is not Hindu.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Poseidon: The Greek god of the sea and earthquakes carried a trident, and belongs to Greek religion.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Freya: Norse goddess of love and war who rode a chariot pulled by cats. Friday is thought to be named for her or Frigg.
Hindu gods and goddesses.Apollo: Greek god of music, prophecy and the sun, he is not Hindu, though he shares a sun role with Surya.
